child: Ask {member} to join you for {activity}.
adult: Invite {member} to join you for {activity} this week.

child: Ask {member} to teach you about {theirActivity}, or do it together.
adult: Join {member} in {theirActivity} – let them lead and teach you.

child: Have 15 minutes of special time with {member} – they choose what to do, no phones!
adult: Give {member} 15 minutes of special time: they choose, you follow, no phones.

child: Go for a walk with {member} and spot 5 interesting things.
adult: Go for a walk with {member}. Let the conversation wander wherever it goes.

child: Cook or bake something with {member}.
adult: Cook a meal together with {member} – one picks the recipe, the other is the helper.

child: Look through old photos with {member}. Find the funniest one!
adult: Look through old photos with {member} and share the stories behind them.

child: Help {member} with one of their jobs today, without being asked.
adult: Help {member} with one of their chores today without being asked.

child: Watch a movie with {member} – all phones in a basket!
adult: Watch a movie with {member} with both phones away. Talk about it afterwards.

child: Make breakfast with {member} for the whole family.
adult: Make a slow weekend breakfast with {member} for the household.

child: Make a family playlist with {member} – each add 3 songs.
adult: Start a family playlist with {member} – each add songs and explain one of them.

child: Plan the family week with {member} on a big piece of paper.
adult: Sit down with {member} and plan the week – include one thing each of you is looking forward to.

child: Plant a seed with {member} and look after it together.
adult: Start something that grows with {member} – a herb pot or a vegetable patch.

child: Make a family 'bucket list' with {member}.
adult: Write a bucket list with {member} and do the first small thing on it.

child: Give {member} a 'yes hour' – you say yes to their (sensible) ideas!
adult: Give {member} a 'yes hour': you say yes to their reasonable ideas for an hour.

child: Watch the sunset or look at the stars with {member}.
adult: Watch a sunset or stargaze with {member}. Leave the phones inside.

child: Make breakfast in bed for {member}.
adult: Surprise {member} with breakfast or coffee in bed.

child: Plan a special day out with {member} – you choose where to go!
adult: Plan a special outing with {member} – you choose where – and go on it together.

child: Wash the car or tidy the garden with {member} and play music while you do it.
adult: Turn a chore into time together: wash the car or garden with {member}, with music on.

child: Read a story or a chapter of a book with {member}.
adult: Read to each other or listen to a podcast episode with {member}, then talk about it.

child: Ask {member} to show you {theirActivity} and have a go yourself.
adult: Go along to something {member} enjoys – {theirActivity} – and take part.

child: At bedtime, tell {member} the best and the trickiest part of your day. Then listen to theirs.
adult: At bedtime, swap the best and hardest part of today with {member}. Just listen – no fixing.

child: Make {member} a cup of tea or a glass of juice and sit together for 10 minutes.
adult: Have your morning coffee or tea with {member} – sit together for ten minutes before the day starts.

child: In the car, bus or taxi with {member}, play 'Would you rather?' the whole way.
adult: On your next car, bus or taxi ride with {member}, play 'would you rather' instead of scrolling.

child: Help {member} get a braai ready – set out the plates and pick the music together.
adult: Have a braai with {member} – get the fire going together and let them be in charge of one part of the meal.

child: Help {member} make a potjie. You can wash the veggies and stir!
adult: Make a potjie with {member} – chop, stir and wait for it together, then dish up for the household.

child: Bake rusks with {member}. Dunk the first ones in tea or milk!
adult: Bake a batch of rusks with {member} and dunk the first ones in tea together.

child: When the power goes off, sit with {member} by torchlight and make up a story together, one sentence each.
adult: During load-shedding, sit with {member} by candle or torchlight and build a made-up story together, one sentence each.

child: Make shadow puppets on the wall with {member} using a torch.
adult: Put on a shadow-puppet show with {member} using a torch and a wall – each invent a character.

child: Go to the shop with {member} and be in charge of finding three things on the list.
adult: Do a shop run with {member}: split the list and race to find your half first.

child: Play a card game with {member}. Teach them one or let them teach you!
adult: Teach {member} a card game you know, or let them teach you one, and play a few rounds.

child: Have a picnic with {member} – on the lounge floor or in the garden!
adult: Pack a simple picnic with {member} and eat it together – the garden, the stoep or a park all count.

child: Have a 3-song dance party with {member} in the kitchen.
adult: Put on three songs and dance in the kitchen with {member} – silliness encouraged.

child: Do a puzzle with {member} – find all the edge pieces first!
adult: Start a jigsaw or crossword with {member} and work on it together for half an hour.

child: Build a blanket fort with {member} and have a snack inside.
adult: Build a blanket fort with {member} and spend some time inside it – snacks and torch optional.

child: Wash up after supper with {member} – one washes, one dries.
adult: Wash and dry the dishes with {member} after supper and use the time to chat.

child: Eat supper with {member} with no TV or phones. Each tell one thing from your day.
adult: Eat supper at the table with {member} with no phones or TV, and each share one thing from your day.

child: Teach {member} something you can do, like a dance move or a trick.
adult: Teach {member} something you're good at – a recipe, a knot, a card trick – and let them try it.

child: Show {member} how you do {activity} and let them have a go.
adult: Show {member} why you love {activity} – explain one thing about it and let them try.

child: Ask {member} about {theirActivity}. Think of three questions to ask!
adult: Ask {member} to tell you about {theirActivity} for ten minutes – ask questions and really listen.

child: Draw one picture together with {member} – take turns adding to it.
adult: Make one drawing together with {member}, taking turns to add a line or shape until it's done.

child: Take some silly photos with {member} and choose your favourite.
adult: Have a silly photo shoot with {member} – pull faces, use props – and choose one favourite to keep.

child: Make a time capsule with {member}. Each put in a note or a small treasure.
adult: Make a time capsule with {member}: each add a note or object, seal it and pick a date to open it.

child: Make a picture on the ground with {member} using leaves, stones and flowers.
adult: Make a nature picture with {member} from leaves, stones and flowers you find outside.

child: Play catch or kick a ball with {member} outside.
adult: Kick a ball, shoot hoops or play catch with {member} outside for 15 minutes.

child: Lie on the grass with {member} and find shapes in the clouds.
adult: Lie on the grass or a blanket with {member} and find shapes in the clouds together.

child: Ask {member} to go swimming with you at a pool or beach with a lifeguard.
adult: Go to a public pool, dam or beach with {member} and get in the water together.

child: Go to a market with {member}. Each choose one thing to taste!
adult: Explore a local market with {member} – each pick one small thing to try or buy.

child: Go to the library with {member} and choose a book for each other.
adult: Visit the library with {member} and each choose a book for the other to read.

child: Go for an ice cream with {member} – just the two of you!
adult: Go for an ice cream or a milkshake with {member}, just the two of you.

child: Plan a special evening for {member}.
adult: Have a date night at home with {member}: candles, a meal you made, and no talk about bills or chores.

child: Go for a walk with {member} and talk.
adult: Go for a coffee walk with {member} and talk about something other than the kids, work or the house.

child: Dance with {member} to a favourite song.
adult: Slow-dance with {member} in the lounge to a song that means something to you both.

child: Ask {member} to show you a video or song they love, and watch it with them.
adult: Ask {member} to show you a video or song they love, and actually watch or listen with them.

child: Play a video game {member} likes. Let them show you how!
adult: Play a video game {member} likes – let them teach you, and don't mind losing.

child: On your next car trip with {member}, take turns choosing the songs.
adult: On your next drive with {member}, let them be the DJ and ask why they chose each song.

child: Fix something broken at home with {member}, like a toy or a wobbly chair.
adult: Fix something broken in the house with {member} – a wobbly chair, a bike tyre, a loose button.

child: Tidy one drawer with {member}. What funny things can you find?
adult: Sort out one cupboard or drawer with {member} and laugh at what you find in it.

child: Have a pamper time with {member} – brush hair, paint nails or play hairdresser.
adult: Have a pamper session with {member} – plait or brush hair, paint nails or do face masks.

child: Do a taste test with {member}. Close your eyes and guess the food!
adult: Do a blind taste test with {member} – each pick four things from the kitchen and guess with eyes closed.

child: Tell {member} your best jokes. Can you make them laugh?
adult: Swap jokes with {member} until one of you laughs out loud – bad jokes count double.

child: Write {member} a note about your favourite time together.
adult: Write {member} a note about a favourite time you've spent together, and suggest doing it again.

child: Write {member} an invitation to play with you. Then play!
adult: Write {member} an invitation to spend time with you – say what, when and where – then do it.

child: Ask {member} five questions, like 'What is your best memory?' Then they ask you.
adult: Ask {member} five questions you've never asked them before, then let them ask you five.

child: Learn the words to a song with {member} and sing it together, loud!
adult: Learn the words to a song with {member} and sing it together, as loudly as you like.

child: Make paper aeroplanes with {member}. Whose flies furthest?
adult: Fold paper aeroplanes with {member} and have a contest to see whose flies furthest.

child: Do some stretches or star jumps with {member}. Take turns being the coach!
adult: Do a short workout or stretch with {member} – one leads for five minutes, then swap.

child: Build something with {member} out of blocks, Lego or boxes.
adult: Build something with {member} out of Lego, blocks, boxes or scrap wood – decide together what it is.

child: Make a family flag with {member}. What should be on it?
adult: Design a family flag or crest with {member} that shows what your household is about.

child: Have a water fight with {member} on a hot day, with sponges and a bucket.
adult: Have a sponge-and-bucket water fight with {member} on a hot day.

child: Ask {member} what they liked to eat when they were little, and make it together.
adult: Ask {member} to teach you a dish they loved growing up, and cook it together.

child: Sit outside with {member}. How many different birds can you see or hear?
adult: Sit outside with {member} for 15 minutes and count how many different birds you can see or hear.

child: Explore a new park or nature spot with {member}.
adult: Explore a park or nature reserve you've never been to with {member} – take a snack along.

child: Go and watch a sports match with {member} and cheer together.
adult: Go and watch a local sports match with {member} and cheer for the same side.

child: Walk to school or the bus stop with {member} and chat on the way.
adult: Walk with {member} to school, the bus stop or the taxi rank and chat on the way.

child: Choose a little weekly thing to do with {member}, like Friday toasties. Do it this week!
adult: Pick a small weekly ritual with {member} – Friday toasted sandwiches, a Sunday walk – and do the first one.

child: Learn 5 words in a new language with {member}, like isiZulu or Afrikaans.
adult: Learn a few words of another South African language with {member} and use them on each other all day.

child: Make a happy jar with {member}. Each write 3 good things from this week.
adult: Make a highlights jar with {member}: each write three good moments from this week and read them out together.

child: Make a little book with {member}. One writes the story, one draws the pictures.
adult: Make a little book with {member} – one writes the story, the other draws the pictures.

child: Hide a small treat and give {member} clues to find it. Then swap!
adult: Hide a small treat and give {member} clues to find it – then swap and let them hide one.

child: Play hide and seek with {member}.
adult: Play hide-and-seek with {member} – yes, adults hide too, and no peeking.
